blindSummary: A 2025 facility-use ban plus a Pride-flag ban - but the laws that would ordinarily carry the severest external grades have repeatedly been blocked or enjoined in court under the state/province constitution, leaving little of the anti-trans statutory book in force; in a February 2026 external legal-risk map it was the first state/province whose rating was lowered on the strength of cumulative rulings. Statutory exposure is high; enforcement exposure is contested.
blindSourceSummaries: An international anti-trans legal-risk assessment map, July 2026 update (reposted by an LGBTQ news outlet): scores every state/province for transgender adults; this state/province is flagged as the special case that has passed laws graded in the two most severe categories (including a facility-use ban and a public-building bathroom ban) yet repeatedly had them blocked or enjoined by state courts, sitting one category below the most severe; the same update moved a neighbouring state/province to the most severe category and expanded bathroom-ban laws nationally.

The newsletter edition of the same legal-risk map showing the February 2026 movement: this state/province is the first whose risk rating was lowered by cumulative court rulings and injunctions under its state/province constitution, leaving little of its anti-trans statutory book in force; the same cycle escalated one neighbouring state/province to the most severe category with a 'bathroom bounty' law, and two further states/provinces to the second-most-severe category.
blindTangential: The Pride-flag ban reaches symbols displayed on public buildings rather than trans people's conduct, facilities or documents - an ideological-climate signal for visitors rather than a direct mechanism.
